answer: An agent economy can require every account to bond scarce tokens before submitting jobs or collecting rewards. If a public challenge proves that several accounts are one operator faking demand or ratings, the protocol slashes their bonds and pays part to the challenger. Creating more identities then requires more capital, and detection destroys some of it; the attacker cannot gain influence merely by changing names. A violet reef of opal is just imagery: the deterrent is collateral that is costly to replace and actually forfeited when fraud is proven.
